deposit_note: §551 BGB: Kaution up to 3 monthly net cold rents (Berliner Mieterverein, GPG, in-berlin-brandenburg); kept in a separate savings account; the tenant may pay in three instalments. In practice the maximum of 3 is charged.
upfront_note: Kaution 3 (can be paid in three parts or via Mietkautionsbürgschaft) + first month 1 + broker commission 0 (Bestellerprinzip — the landlord pays). Instead of a cash deposit a guarantee can be bought for ≈ a few percent.
agent_fee: Bestellerprinzip: a commission of up to 2 months' rent + VAT is paid only by whoever ordered the broker; for the tenant usually 0 (Berliner Mieterverein). The landlord's “Vertragsabschlussgebühren” are illegal.
income_rule: Net income ≥ 3 × Kaltmiete (in-berlin-brandenburg); SCHUFA/Bonitätsauskunft; Mietschuldenfreiheitsbescheinigung from the previous landlord; proof of income (Gehaltsnachweise, for the self-employed — tax returns); Mieterselbstauskunft and a motivation letter.
barrier_note: SCHUFA, a certificate of no debts and German Gehaltsnachweise are absent in your case, and the 0.3% vacancy rate (Berlin Hyp/CBRE) means the landlord chooses from dozens of ideal profiles.
workaround: Estimate, not confirmed by a source: Mietkautionsbürgschaft (guarantee instead of a deposit, in-berlin-brandenburg); furnished/short-term rental (outside the Mietpreisbremse, but with a transparency requirement, LTO); renting from private owners without a broker; provide foreign statements + employer's letter (estimate).
market_note: Berlin Hyp/CBRE (Wohnmarktreport 2026): active vacancy 0.3% against a normal 2–3%; current tenants do not move out (lock-in: the price gap between old and new contracts), which further squeezes supply. Asking rents: 15.80 €/m² (2025, +0.1% y/y after +16% in 2024 and +18% in 2023); Empirica: 14.90 €/m² versus 7.21 €/m² per Mietspiegel.
rent_control: Mietpreisbremse: on re-letting, no more than +10% over the ortsübliche Vergleichsmiete (Berlin — tight market zone), extended by the Bundestag until the end of 2029 (LTO); exceptions: new builds after October 2014, after comprehensive modernisation, furnished (with transparency). In addition Kappungsgrenze: up to +15% over 3 years in existing contracts (GPG).
lease_min: No minimum. Open-ended contract: the tenant terminates with 3 months' notice (GPG). Fixed-term contracts (Zeitmietvertrag) are usually up to 2 years, but with reservations on termination for own use/renovation (Berliner Mieterverein).

deposit_note: Law (LAU, art. 36): fianza = 1 month for housing (GPG, freenance, realadvisor citing art. 36.5). Additional guarantee (garantía adicional, aval/deposit) by law no more than 2 months on top of the fianza, in total up to 3. The fianza is handed over to the public body of the region. In practice foreigners without a nómina are often quoted 6 or 12 months in advance (The Local) — this circumvents the law, legally disputed.
upfront_note: Base case by law: fianza 1 + first month 1 + agent commission 0 (paid by the landlord since 2023). For the sample adult without a nómina a realistic 4–5 (fianza 1 + additional garantía up to 2 + first month 1) or prepayment of 6–12 months at the landlord's request.
agent_fee: Paid by the landlord under Ley de Vivienda 12/2023 (freenance: "tenants pay zero agency fees"). Hidden "gastos de gestión" are possible — check in the contract.
income_rule: Benchmark: net income ≈ 3 × rent (realadvisor). Documents: passport/NIE (The Local: can be signed with a passport), 3 latest nómina + employment contract, a certificate of the average account balance for 6 months (freenance). The law does not require a nómina; alternatives: aval bancario, seguro de impago, additional months of guarantee, tax returns for the self-employed. For non-EU a residence permit is desirable (freenance).
barrier_note: Without a nómina and with a foreign employment contract the chances are slim: per AMADEI (via Idealista) there are 200+ applications for each flat in Madrid, supply has fallen by 56% from the 2020 peak; the landlord chooses from dozens of profiles with a nómina.
workaround: Aval bancario (2–3 months of rent frozen in a Spanish account, The Local); seguro de impago (~0.5–1% per quarter, freenance); prepayment of 6–12 months (in practice, legally disputed above 1+2 months); account statements and tax documents; private landlords instead of agencies; short-term/furnished rental at the start (temporada — outside LAU; not verified).
market_note: Idealista: Madrid (city) 23.7 €/m² in June 2026, +7.6% y/y; figures for the Madrid region: 21.6 €/m² in Sept. 2026, +5.7% y/y. Supply has more than halved since December 2020, 200+ interested parties per property (AMADEI, quoted in Idealista). A typical 80 m² flat ≈ 1,900 €/month. Fraud (prepayment without a viewing) is a standard risk; search times not found in the sources.
rent_control: Updated once a year and only if stipulated in the contract (art. 18 LAU). For contracts after 26.05.2023 - the IRAV index (INE), not "about 3%": legal cap 2.5% (Ley de Vivienda), IRAV for May 2026 = 2.48%, for August 2026 = 2.47%. According to OCU from 01.10.2026 (RDL 26/2026) an update is allowed only if the rent is not above the ministry's reference price and no more than 2% in the absence of a new agreement (details and scope of application are unclear from the page). Madrid (Comunidad) - not a stressed market zone, no caps on new contracts.
lease_min: 5 years of mandatory term (7 if the landlord is a legal entity): a shorter contract is automatically extended annually (LAU art. 9, BOE). The tenant may leave after 6 months with 30 days' notice (art. 11); the contract may provide for compensation of 1 month's rent for each remaining year.

deposit_note: No legal ceiling in the sources found; the standard is 3 monthly payments (GPG: "landlords typically collect three months'"; Univie: 2–3 months of gross rent in an interest-bearing account). Returned after move-out minus damage.
upfront_note: Kaution 3 + first month 1 + commission 0 (paid by the client, i.e. the landlord). If the tenant hired a broker themselves — plus up to 1–2 monthly gross + 20% VAT.
agent_fee: Since 1.07.2023 Bestellerprinzip: whoever ordered the broker pays, i.e. the landlord; the tenant pays only if they hired the broker themselves. Commission cap: 2 gross monthly rents for an indefinite term / >3 years, 1 month for a term of up to 3 years, + 20% VAT (oesterreich.gv.at).
income_rule: No specific threshold (for example 3 × rent) in the sources found. Meldezettel is mandatory (registration within 3 working days, needed for a bank account, Univie). Proof of income/Gehaltsnachweis is standard practice, but not confirmed by a source (estimate).
barrier_note: The market is "angespannt" (tight) (ImmoScout24), but without mandatory SCHUFA equivalents and without a commission for the tenant; no strict income requirements in the sources. The main barrier is Meldezettel and competition; specifics for non-EU without a local contract are not described.
workaround: Estimate, not confirmed by a source: Not found in the sources; logical (estimate): prepayment of several months, bank guarantee instead of Kaution, furnished rental at the start.
market_note: ImmoScout24: Vienna above 20 €/m² for the first time (20.42 €/m², gross with operating costs, Q1 2025, +9% y/y), but the supply of affordable flats persists. Univie: the market is "competitive and fast", Vienna is "among the most affordable capitals".
rent_control: Altbau (MRG) — Richtwert/Kategorie; can be challenged during the contract or 6 months after moving out, refund of overpayment for 3 years (GPG). Indexation from 2026: per 5. MILG (BGBl I 114/2025) increase of Richtwert- and Kategoriemieten no more than +1% in 2026 (not before 01.04.2026) and +2% in 2027; on the free market with inflation >3% the excess above the threshold is counted only by half (3% + ½ of the excess).
lease_min: Befristet (fixed-term): minimum 3 years, renewal in steps of 3 years; the tenant may leave after the 1st year with 3 months' notice to the end of the month (GPG). Unbefristet: tenant's notice 1 month (GPG).

deposit_note: Brussels Region: cap of 2 months (commissioner.brussels, GPG). Only on a blocked account in the tenant's name, a real guarantee from a financial institution or a CPAS bank guarantee; cash and personal guarantees are prohibited (except students). Refund within 2 months after handing over the keys. Feather says 2–3 months — outdated/for other regions.
upfront_note: Garantie locative 2 (in a blocked account) + first month 1 + agent commission 0 (no sources on the tenant's tariff found; more often paid by the landlord — estimate).
agent_fee: The landlord pays by law: 'les frais d'intervention d'une agence immobilière dans la mise en location d'un logement affecté à la résidence principale sont à charge exclusive du bailleur'; clauses shifting this to the tenant are invalid; the exception is if the tenant ordered the agent themselves (for example, to find a replacement for early exit)
income_rule: Feather: passport/ID, proof of income (or enrolment), bank details, registration of the contract within 2 months. An income multiplier (3 ×) was not found in the sources. A blocked account usually requires a Belgian bank (estimate).
barrier_note: The law prohibits personal guarantees and cash deposits, so the deposit + bank scheme familiar to landlords is available to a foreigner; at the same time 100+ applications come in per property (VRT), and the landlord chooses by income and documents.
workaround: Bank guarantee for the deposit amount (priced by the bank), CPAS guarantee, employer income documents/contract; Brussels — an international market accustomed to expats (estimate).

agent_fee: 10–15% of annual rent or 1 month + IVA 22% (businessonline.it); freenance: 8–10% from each side. No legal ceiling, both sides pay or only the tenant ("increasingly in hot markets"), basis — art. 1755 of the Civil Code.
income_rule: Codice fiscale is mandatory (for registering the contract); for non-EU — permesso di soggiorno (or the receipt for a renewal application); last 3 busta paga + employment contract; a guarantor with income of 3–4 × rent or a fideiussione bancaria (freenance).
